matter_reference_date_basis: exam session of the source paper (OCTOBER 2021); the proposed mortgage to National Savings Bank is contemplated as at that session, so the law is taken as it stood in October 2021.
corpus_gaps: The National Savings Bank Act, No. 30 of 1971 is not in the corpus, so the corporate identity of the National Savings Bank is taken only from the list in Mortgage Act s.47A(7)(d), not from its own constitutive Act.

The Mortgage (Amendment) Act, No. 3 of 1990, which inserted s.47A and substituted s.46, is not a separate document in the corpus; its effect is visible only through the amendment_events recorded on the consolidated Mortgage Act sections.

No monetary-threshold updating instrument for the 'one hundred and fifty thousand rupees' figure in s.47A(1) is present in the corpus; the researcher found no later amendment of that figure, but the corpus cannot positively rule one out.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: Where at the time of the execution of a mortgage bond in favour of a lending institution for the payment of a loan, the principal of which exceeds one hundred and fifty thousand rupees the mortgagor executes a separate instrument, attested by the notary attesting the bond and by the witnesses to the bond containing- (a) a special declaration on the part of the mortgagor that he renounces the benefit of section 46 and that the effect of such renunciation has been explained to him by the notary
provisions.why_relevant: This is the provision the Bank's requested declaration is executed under. It is the only route by which a mortgagor's property other than the mortgaged land can be made liable under a decree on the mortgage: a separate instrument, executed at the time of the bond, containing a special declaration renouncing the benefit of section 46. It also sets the two gateway conditions - a lending institution as mortgagee and a loan principal exceeding Rs.150,000.
provisions.temporal_note: Inserted by Act No. 3 of 1990 and in force from 1990; no later amendment event is recorded on this section in the corpus. It is therefore in force at the matter reference date of October 2021. Subsection (6) excludes mortgages created before the section came into force, which does not affect a mortgage to be created in 2021.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: No decree in any hypothecary action upon any mortgage of land which is created after the coming into force of this section, and no decree in any action for the recovery of any moneys due upon any such mortgage, shall order any property, whatsoever, other than the mortgaged property to be sold for the recovery of any money found to be due under the mortgage, and no property whatsoever, other than the mortgaged property, shall be sold or be liable to be sold in execution of any such decree.
provisions.why_relevant: This is the benefit that the s.47A declaration renounces, and it explains the Bank's motive. Without a renunciation the Bank's recovery on a decree is confined to the mortgaged Rajagiriya land; if that land realises less than the debt, the shortfall cannot be recovered against the mortgagor's other property.
provisions.temporal_note: Substituted by Act No. 3 of 1990; latest recorded change 1990, so the substituted text is the text in force at October 2021.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: For the purpose of this section 'lending institution' means- (a) a licensed Commercial Bank within the meaning of the Banking Act, No.30 of 1988; (b) the State Mortgage and Investment Bank established by the State Mortgage and Investment Bank Act, No. 13 of 1975; (c) the National Development Bank established by the National Development Bank of Sri Lanka Act, No. 2 of 1979; (d) the National Savings Bank established by the National Savings Bank Act, No. 30 of 1971;
provisions.why_relevant: Section 47A is available only to a 'lending institution' as defined here. Paragraph (d) names the National Savings Bank expressly, so the mortgagee in this scenario falls squarely within the definition and the section is capable of applying to the proposed bond.
provisions.temporal_note: Part of s.47A as inserted in 1990; no later amendment event recorded. The footnote reference to section 2 of Act No. 23 of 1997 in paragraph (e) concerns the DFCC Bank only and does not bear on paragraph (d).

provisions.relevant_excerpt: then, in addition to the mortgaged property, any other property belonging to the mortgagor shall, subject To the provisions of subsection(2), be liable to be ordered to be sold and to be sold under the decree in an action upon the mortgage, and the provisions of section 218 of the Civil Procedure Code (Chapter 101) shall, mutatis mutandis, apply to the seizure and sale of such other property.
provisions.why_relevant: States the consequence the Bank is buying with the declaration: property of the mortgagor beyond the mortgaged land becomes liable to be ordered sold under the decree, with Civil Procedure Code s.218 applied to the seizure and sale.
provisions.temporal_note: Same insertion by Act No. 3 of 1990; in force at October 2021. The corpus text reproduces the printed capitalisation 'subject To' and the unspaced 'subsection(2)'.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: no process shall issue for the seizure and sale of any property of the mortgagor, other than the mortgaged property, until the mortgaged property is sold and the proceeds thereof applied in satisfaction of the decree.
provisions.why_relevant: Qualifies the extended remedy: the Bank must first sell the mortgaged land and apply the proceeds before touching other property. It confirms that the declaration is a shortfall-recovery device rather than a free choice of assets, which is why the Bank wants it at the outset.
provisions.temporal_note: Same insertion by Act No. 3 of 1990; in force at October 2021.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: it shall be the duty of the notary to explain to the mortgagor, that the instrument provides for the renunciation of the benefit of section 46 and that the effect of such renunciation is that, in addition to the mortgaged property, other property of the mortgagor is liable to be sold in execution of a decree in an action upon the mortgage.
provisions.why_relevant: Explains why the Bank asks for a separate signed instrument attested and endorsed by the notary rather than a clause buried in the bond: the renunciation is only effective if the notary has explained it and endorsed that fact, so the formality is what makes the Bank's extended remedy secure.
provisions.temporal_note: Same insertion by Act No. 3 of 1990; in force at October 2021.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: The provisions of section 46 shall have effect notwithstanding anything in any other law or in any mortgage bond or other instrument.
provisions.why_relevant: Shows that the section 46 restriction cannot be contracted out of by a term in the bond itself, which is why the Bank must use the specific statutory mechanism of a separate s.47A instrument instead of simply drafting a wider recovery clause into the mortgage bond.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1949 with no recorded later change; in force at October 2021.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: the judgment-creditor has the power to seize, and to sell or realize in money by the hands of the Fiscal, except as hereinafter mentioned, all saleable property, movable or immovable, belonging to the judgment-debtor
provisions.why_relevant: Background only: the machinery that s.47A(1) applies mutatis mutandis to the seizure and sale of the mortgagor's other property once the benefit of s.46 has been renounced, together with the protected categories in its proviso.
provisions.temporal_note: In force from 1889, latest recorded change 1977; in force at October 2021.
provisions.verifier_note: Excerpt and background role confirmed, but it stops before the proviso to section 218, which exempts listed property from seizure and sale - including, under paragraph (n), an unmortgaged house that is the judgment-debtor's actual residence - so the extended remedy the declaration unlocks does not reach every asset of the mortgagor.

provisions.relevant_excerpt: (b) an endorsement signed by the notary to the effect that he has explained to the mortgagor the effect of such renunciation
provisions.why_relevant: Added by the verifier. The separate instrument is effective only if it contains both the mortgagor's declaration in paragraph (a) and the notary's signed endorsement in paragraph (b). The researcher's excerpt for PROV-M059-001 stops at the end of paragraph (a), yet claim CL-M059-Q01-003 and the rule part of the gold answer both assert the endorsement requirement, so it needed its own cited text.
provisions.temporal_note: Part of section 47A as inserted by Act No. 3 of 1990; no later amendment event is recorded on the section in the corpus, so it is in force at October 2021.

questions.authority_requirement_reason: The question asks for the Bank's reason for requiring a declaration expressly identified as one under section 47A of the Mortgage Act. The reason is written into the statute itself: s.46 confines recovery under a mortgage decree to the mortgaged property, and s.47A is the sole statutory mechanism by which that benefit can be renounced so that the mortgagor's other property becomes liable. The conditions (lending institution, principal over Rs.150,000, separate notarially attested instrument) and the consequence are all on the face of the Act, and s.47 shows the restriction cannot be displaced by contract. No judicial authority or Roman-Dutch doctrine is needed for a complete answer.

legal_issues.issue: What, under the Mortgage Act, is the legal effect of a mortgagor executing a separate declaration under section 47A at the execution of a mortgage bond?
What is the default position under section 46 that such a declaration renounces, and can a lender achieve the same result without it?
Are the statutory gateway conditions of section 47A satisfied on these facts, namely a lending institution as mortgagee and a loan principal exceeding one hundred and fifty thousand rupees?

questions.hop_count_basis: Three necessary linked steps: (1) s.46 restricts a mortgage decree to the mortgaged property; (2) s.47A(1) permits that benefit to be renounced by a separate declaration and states the resulting liability of other property; (3) the s.47A(7) definition of 'lending institution' must be satisfied for the section to apply at all, and paragraph (d) names the National Savings Bank. The s.47A(1) closing words are counted with step (2) as the same provision's operative consequence rather than as a separate hop. Verifier: retained at 3. The section 47A(7) 'lending institution' gateway is counted as its own hop because it is a separate definitional lookup that the section's application depends on; counting it inside step (2) would give 2, and either reading is defensible. The added PROV-M059-901 (section 47A(1)(b) endorsement) is a formality within step (2), not a further hop.

enrichment.original_background:
Lihini Manapitiya, a lecturer of AVI University purchased a land situated in Rajagiriya in 2001 for Rs.14,000,000/-. She wishes to obtain a loan of Rupees Two Million (Rs.2,000,000/=) from National Savings Bank to build a house.

Lihini Manapitiya was asked to sign a Declaration under section 47(A) of the Mortgage Act by the Bank.

gold_answer_draft.issue: Why does the National Savings Bank ask Lihini Manapitiya to execute a separate declaration under section 47A of the Mortgage Act at the time she mortgages her Rajagiriya land to secure the Rs.2,000,000 housing loan?
gold_answer_draft.rule: Mortgage Act s.46 provides that no decree in a hypothecary action on a mortgage of land, and no decree in an action for the recovery of moneys due on such a mortgage, may order any property other than the mortgaged property to be sold, and no other property is liable to be sold in execution of such a decree. By s.47 that restriction operates notwithstanding anything in any other law or in any mortgage bond or other instrument, so a lender cannot escape it by a clause in the bond. Section 47A creates the single statutory exception. Where, at the time of execution of a mortgage bond in favour of a lending institution for a loan the principal of which exceeds one hundred and fifty thousand rupees, the mortgagor executes a separate instrument attested by the notary attesting the bond and by the witnesses to it, containing a special declaration renouncing the benefit of s.46 together with the notary's endorsement that he has explained the effect of the renunciation, then in addition to the mortgaged property any other property belonging to the mortgagor becomes liable to be ordered to be sold and to be sold under the decree in an action upon the mortgage, with Civil Procedure Code s.218 applying mutatis mutandis to the seizure and sale of that other property. Section 47A(7)(d) includes the National Savings Bank in the definition of 'lending institution'. Section 47A(2) requires that no process issue against other property until the mortgaged property has been sold and its proceeds applied to the decree, and s.47A(3) makes it the notary's duty to explain the renunciation and its consequences to the mortgagor.
gold_answer_draft.application: The mortgagee is the National Savings Bank, which is a lending institution within Mortgage Act s.47A(7)(d). The principal of the loan is Rs.2,000,000, which exceeds the statutory threshold of one hundred and fifty thousand rupees in s.47A(1). Both gateway conditions are therefore met and the section is available on these facts. Absent the declaration, s.46 would confine the Bank on any decree obtained on the bond to the Rajagiriya land alone, and by s.47 the Bank could not enlarge its remedy by drafting a wider recovery clause into the bond itself. By asking Lihini Manapitiya to sign a separate instrument under s.47A renouncing the benefit of s.46, the Bank secures the right, if the debt is not satisfied, to have her other property ordered sold under the decree in an action upon the mortgage, the seizure and sale being governed mutatis mutandis by Civil Procedure Code s.218. That right is a shortfall remedy rather than a free choice of assets, since s.47A(2) bars process against her other property until the mortgaged land is sold and the proceeds applied. The instrument must be separate, attested by the same notary and witnesses, and carry the notary's endorsement, and under s.47A(3) the notary must explain to her that she is giving up the s.46 protection.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The Bank requests the declaration in order to escape the restriction in Mortgage Act s.46, which would otherwise limit its recovery on a mortgage decree to the mortgaged Rajagiriya land. Because the National Savings Bank is a lending institution under s.47A(7)(d) and the Rs.2,000,000 principal exceeds the Rs.150,000 threshold, a declaration executed under s.47A(1) renouncing the benefit of s.46 makes Lihini Manapitiya's other property liable to be sold under a decree in an action upon the mortgage, subject to the mortgaged land being sold first under s.47A(2). In short, the Bank wants recourse against her general assets for any shortfall, and s.47A is the only lawful way to obtain it. Whether that recourse is ever exercised depends on facts not given, namely what other property she owns and whether the mortgaged land would realise enough to satisfy the debt.

answer_claims.claim_text: Under Mortgage Act s.46, a decree in a hypothecary action on a mortgage of land, or in an action to recover moneys due on such a mortgage, cannot order any property other than the mortgaged property to be sold, and no other property is liable to be sold in execution of such a decree.
By Mortgage Act s.47 the s.46 restriction has effect notwithstanding anything in any other law or in any mortgage bond or other instrument, so a lender cannot displace it by a term of the bond.

Mortgage Act s.47A(1) allows the benefit of s.46 to be renounced where, at the time of execution of a mortgage bond in favour of a lending institution for a loan whose principal exceeds one hundred and fifty thousand rupees, the mortgagor executes a separate instrument attested by the notary attesting the bond and by the witnesses to it, containing a special declaration of renunciation and the notary's endorsement that he explained its effect.

Where such an instrument is executed, in addition to the mortgaged property any other property belonging to the mortgagor is liable to be ordered to be sold and to be sold under the decree in an action upon the mortgage, and Civil Procedure Code s.218 applies mutatis mutandis to the seizure and sale of that other property.
Mortgage Act s.47A(2) prevents process issuing against the mortgagor's other property until the mortgaged property has been sold and the proceeds applied in satisfaction of the decree.

Mortgage Act s.47A(3) imposes a duty on the notary to explain to the mortgagor that the instrument renounces the benefit of s.46 and that other property becomes liable to be sold in execution of a decree on the mortgage.
The National Savings Bank, the proposed mortgagee, is a lending institution for the purposes of s.47A because s.47A(7)(d) names it expressly.
The principal of the loan, Rs.2,000,000, exceeds the one hundred and fifty thousand rupee threshold in s.47A(1), so the section is available on these facts.
Without the declaration the Bank's recovery under any decree on the bond would be confined to the mortgaged Rajagiriya land, and it could not enlarge that remedy by a clause in the bond.

The Bank requests the s.47A declaration so that, on the mortgagor renouncing the benefit of s.46, her property other than the mortgaged land becomes liable to be sold under a decree in an action upon the mortgage, giving the Bank recourse for any shortfall.
That recourse is a shortfall remedy only: the Bank must first sell the mortgaged land and apply the proceeds before process may issue against her other property.
